title: ARISCAT Score (Postoperative Pulmonary Complications)
sources: Canet J et al. Anesthesiology 2010 (ARISCAT); PERISCOPE external validation, Eur J Anaesthesiol 2014
purpose: Predicts the risk of in-hospital postoperative pulmonary complications (respiratory failure, infection, effusion, atelectasis, pneumothorax, bronchospasm, aspiration pneumonitis) after surgery under general or regional anaesthesia.

items.label: Respiratory infection in the last month (fever + antibiotics)

interpretation.label: Low risk — PPC incidence ~ 1.6%. Routine care; standard lung-protective ventilation and early mobilisation

Intermediate risk — PPC incidence ~ 13%. Optimise: treat infection / anaemia pre-op, incentive spirometry, lung-protective ventilation (VT 6–8 mL/kg PBW, PEEP, recruitment), regional analgesia, postoperative CPAP/physiotherapy, consider monitored bed

High risk — PPC incidence ~ 42%. Aggressive optimisation and risk–benefit discussion; strong indication for step-down/ICU, protective ventilation, minimising surgical duration, and a structured respiratory care bundle

notes: SpO2 and incision site carry the most weight — a hypoxaemic patient for a thoracotomy is high-risk almost regardless of the other items. Pair with functional status, an ASA class, and (for cardiac risk) the RCRI. ARISCAT informs consent, anaesthetic technique, ventilation strategy, and disposition — not cancellation by itself.
buildNote: Additive, 7 items with weighted points. Range 0–123.
